boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten campus study settings with documented seating, work surfaces, group space, or academic support.

cards.title: Settle Into Greenley Library
cards.subtitle: Group tables, booths, cubicles, and soft seating
cards.notes: Choose a group table or booth for collaborative work, or move to an individual cubicle when the assignment calls for fewer distractions.
cards.short_summary: A flexible library setting that supports both group sessions and independent work.
cards.evidence_claim: The library states that Greenley provides group tables and booths, individual cubicles, comfortable chairs, Wi-Fi, and group seating that cannot be reserved in advance.
cards.access_notes: Open seven days a week when classes are in session; consult the library homepage for current hours. Group spaces are not reservable in advance.

cards.title: Work From the School of Business
cards.subtitle: Lounge areas distributed across all three floors
cards.notes: Pick the floor nearest your next class, then use the lounge seating for reading, reviewing notes, or meeting a project partner.
cards.short_summary: Three floors of lounge options make it practical to fit study time between business classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Farmingdale State College's Academic Advisement Handbook identifies lounge areas with vending machines on all three floors of the School of Business as places to study and meet.
cards.access_notes: Use during normal campus-building access. The cited handbook does not state separate lounge hours or reservation requirements.

cards.title: Take Your Notes Outside at Bunche Plaza
cards.subtitle: Outdoor benches between Laffin and Greenley halls
cards.notes: Bring material that works without a desk, and use the benches for a short reading block or an outdoor review between nearby classes.
cards.short_summary: A mapped outdoor pause point suited to compact reading and review sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Advisement Handbook lists Bunche Plaza as an outdoor study and meeting area with benches between Laffin and Greenley halls.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor setting; plan around weather and daylight. No reservation process or dedicated operating hours are stated.

cards.title: Claim a Campus Center Lounge Seat
cards.subtitle: Two open lounges near the campus dining spaces
cards.notes: Use an open lounge for a group check-in or laptop task, keeping dining-area activity in mind when choosing the quieter of the two spaces.
cards.short_summary: A central indoor option with two open lounges and nearby campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Advisement Handbook identifies two open lounge areas and two large cafeterias in the Campus Center as places to study and meet.
cards.access_notes: The lounges are described as open areas rather than reservable rooms. Verify current Campus Center access before an early or evening visit.

cards.title: Choose a Floor in Gleeson Hall
cards.subtitle: Second- and third-floor lounges plus lobby counter seating
cards.notes: Try the upper-floor lounges for a longer session, or use the front-lobby counter and stools for a quick laptop task before class.
cards.short_summary: Multiple seating formats support anything from a brief email to a longer work block.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Advisement Handbook documents lounges on Gleeson Hall's second and third floors, plus bar stools and a counter in the front lobby.
cards.access_notes: Use during normal academic-building access. The handbook does not list reservations, dedicated lounge hours, or quiet-zone rules.

cards.title: Pause and Study in Hale Hall
cards.subtitle: First- and second-floor lounge areas
cards.notes: Compare the two floors before settling in, then use the closer lounge to review notes without adding another cross-campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A pair of indoor lounge choices positioned within an academic building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Advisement Handbook lists lounge areas on Hale Hall's first and second floors, with vending machines on the first floor.
cards.access_notes: Use while Hale Hall is accessible for campus activities. No reservation procedure, dedicated hours, or guaranteed seating is documented.

cards.title: Build a Work Block Into Lupton Hall
cards.subtitle: Indoor lounges on both the first and second floors
cards.notes: Use the first-floor lounge for a fast stop or check the second floor when you want to separate your study session from lobby traffic.
cards.short_summary: Two indoor lounge levels offer a practical study stop around Lupton-based classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Advisement Handbook names lounge areas on Lupton Hall's first and second floors, with vending machines on the first floor.
cards.access_notes: Use during normal Lupton Hall access. The cited source does not provide reservations, dedicated lounge hours, or noise restrictions.

cards.title: Spread Out in Roosevelt Hall's Lobby
cards.subtitle: Tables, chairs, benches, and vending nearby
cards.notes: Choose a table for written work or a bench for reading, and keep the central lobby circulation path clear while you study.
cards.short_summary: A lobby with several documented seating types and table space for coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Advisement Handbook identifies Roosevelt Hall's lobby as a study and meeting place with tables, chairs, benches, and vending machines.
cards.access_notes: This is an open building lobby, not a reservable study room. Use during building access and expect ordinary circulation through the space.

cards.title: Drop Into the Pit at Sinclair Hall
cards.subtitle: West-side lounge area with vending machines
cards.notes: Head to Sinclair's west side and use the designated lounge for a focused review session or a planned meetup with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A specifically located Sinclair Hall lounge that is easy to describe to a study partner.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Advisement Handbook lists the lounge area known as the Pit on the west side of Sinclair Hall, noting nearby vending machines.
cards.access_notes: Use during normal Sinclair Hall access. The handbook gives no reservation process, separate operating hours, or quiet designation.

cards.title: Keep the Study Session in Whitman Hall
cards.subtitle: First-floor lounge area with vending nearby
cards.notes: Use the first-floor lounge to review a problem set or organize notes before moving to your next class or scheduled academic-support session.
cards.short_summary: A straightforward first-floor landing spot for short, task-focused study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Advisement Handbook identifies Whitman Hall's first-floor lounge area, with vending machines, as a place to study and meet.
cards.access_notes: Use during normal Whitman Hall access. No lounge reservation procedure, dedicated hours, or guaranteed seating is documented.
